topic: A person learns their childhood best friend doesn't remember them
text: I called out to them, just to see, hoping they'd light up, smile, remember. But it was like... nothing. They saw me, they nodded, a polite stranger's nod. I tried to fill the silence with laughter, with the old jokes, the shared history. It was me, the kid with the bike and the secret hideout. The echo of that silence is deafening. I keep telling myself it's just a memory lapse, it'll come back. I cling to that, even as I find myself talking to myself about the times we had, trying to convince someone, maybe myself, that those moments still mean something. I have to believe they do. That we still do.
